records.source: וַיִּקְחוּ֙ עַם־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֶת־יְהוֹאָחָ֖ז בֶּן־יֹאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ וַיַּמְלִיכֻ֥הוּ תַֽחַת־אָבִ֖יו בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: And took [the] people of the land Jehoahaz son of Josiah, and made him king in place of his father in Jerusalem.
pieces: The people of the land then took Jehoahaz son of Josiah and made him king in Jerusalem to succeed his father.

L.1: And the people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah and made him king in place of his father in Jerusalem.

R.1: After that, the people of the land chose Josiah's son Jehoahaz. They made him king in Jerusalem in his father's place.

decisions.choice: the same words as 2 Kings 23:30b, without the anointing
decisions.reason: Verses 1-10 follow 2 Kings 23:30-24:17 in shortened form. Kings says the people of the land took Jehoahaz "and anointed him and made him king"; Chronicles leaves out the anointing and adds "in Jerusalem". The account of Josiah's death and burial comes just before (35:20-27).

decisions.choice: the people of the land: the citizens of Judah
decisions.reason: As in 23:20-21 and 33:25, the free people of Judah act together to put a king on the throne. They chose Jehoahaz although his brother Eliakim was older (verses 2, 5).

decisions.choice: Jehoahaz: also called Shallum
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 22:11 and 1 Chronicles 3:15 call this son of Josiah Shallum. Jehoahaz may have been the name he took as king.

decisions.choice: the wording of 2 Kings 23:30b
decisions.reason: Each level reuses its wording from 2 Kings 23:30b where the Hebrew is the same, and adds "in Jerusalem" where Chronicles has it.

records.heading: The last kings of Judah

records.source: בֶּן־שָׁל֧וֹשׁ וְעֶשְׂרִ֛ים שָׁנָ֖ה יוֹאָחָ֣ז בְּמָלְכ֑וֹ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה חֳדָשִׁ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: [A] son of three and twenty year[s] [was] Jehoahaz when he became king, and three months he reigned in Jerusalem.
pieces: Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem.

L.2: A son of twenty-three years [was] Jehoahaz when he became king, and three months he reigned in Jerusalem.

R.2: Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for three months.

decisions.choice: 2 Kings 23:31 without the name of his mother
decisions.reason: The age and the length of the reign are the same as in 2 Kings 23:31. Chronicles leaves out his mother, Hamutal, and the verdict on his reign (2 Kings 23:32), as it does for each of the last kings.

decisions.choice: a son of twenty-three years: twenty-three years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being "a son of" so many years.

decisions.choice: Joahaz: a shorter spelling of Jehoahaz
decisions.reason: Here and in verse 4 the name is spelled in its short form, without the first syllable of the divine name. It is the same king as in verse 1.

decisions.choice: the accession formula worded as in 2 Kings 23:31
decisions.reason: Each level reuses the wording of 2 Kings 23:31, so the reader sees that the two books say the same. The short spelling of the name is given in its usual form.

records.source: וַיְסִירֵ֥הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֖יִם בִּֽירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַֽיַּעֲנֹשׁ֙ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ מֵאָ֥ה כִכַּר־כֶּ֖סֶף וְכִכַּ֥ר זָהָֽב׃
records.gloss: And removed him [the] king of Egypt in Jerusalem, and fined the land a hundred talent[s] of silver and a talent of gold.
pieces: The king of Egypt removed him from the throne in Jerusalem and imposed on the land a payment of {{units:about 7,500 pounds|100 talents}} of silver and {{units:about 75 pounds|a talent}} of gold.

L.3: And the king of Egypt removed him in Jerusalem, and he imposed a fine on the land, 100 talents of silver and a talent of gold.

R.3: The king of Egypt took the throne away from him in Jerusalem. He forced the land of Judah to pay {{units:about 7,500 pounds|100 talents}} of silver and {{units:about 75 pounds|a talent}} of gold.

decisions.choice: removed him in Jerusalem: 2 Kings 23:33 says Neco bound him at Riblah
decisions.reason: Kings says Pharaoh Neco put Jehoahaz in bonds at Riblah in the land of Hamath "from reigning in Jerusalem". Chronicles gives the result in one word: the king of Egypt removed him, that is, put an end to his reign in Jerusalem. It does not say where it was done.

decisions.choice: fined: laid a payment on a conquered land
decisions.reason: The verb means to impose a penalty or fine. Judah, now under Egypt, had to pay tribute (2 Kings 23:33, 35).

decisions.choice: a talent: about 75 pounds of metal
decisions.reason: As at 2 Kings 23:33, a talent was the largest weight, about 75 pounds.

decisions.choice: about 7,500 pounds ... about 75 pounds
decisions.reason: As at 2 Kings 23:33: Balanced and Readable give modern weights, with the talents as the alternative; Literal keeps the talents. Balanced adds "from the throne" to say what "removed" means here.

records.source: וַיַּמְלֵ֨ךְ מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֜יִם אֶת־אֶלְיָקִ֣ים אָחִ֗יו עַל־יְהוּדָה֙ וִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַיַּסֵּ֥ב אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ יְהוֹיָקִ֑ים וְאֶת־יוֹאָחָ֤ז אָחִיו֙ לָקַ֣ח נְכ֔וֹ וַיְבִיאֵ֖הוּ מִצְרָֽיְמָה׃פ
records.gloss: And made king [the] king of Egypt Eliakim his brother over Judah and Jerusalem, and changed his name [to] Jehoiakim; and Jehoahaz his brother took Neco, and brought him [to] Egypt.
pieces: The king of Egypt made Eliakim, the brother of Jehoahaz, king over Judah and Jerusalem, and changed Eliakim's name to Jehoiakim. But Neco took Jehoahaz, Eliakim's brother, and brought him to Egypt.

L.4: And the king of Egypt made Eliakim his brother king over Judah and Jerusalem, and changed his name [to] Jehoiakim; and Jehoahaz his brother Neco took, and he brought him [to] Egypt.

R.4: The king of Egypt made Jehoahaz's brother Eliakim king over Judah and Jerusalem. He changed Eliakim's name to Jehoiakim. Neco took Jehoahaz, the new king's brother, away to Egypt.

decisions.choice: 2 Kings 23:34, told from the point of view of the two brothers
decisions.reason: Kings says Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim "son of Josiah" king "in place of Josiah his father", and that Jehoahaz "came to Egypt and died there". Chronicles calls Eliakim "his brother", that is, Jehoahaz's brother, says he was made king "over Judah and Jerusalem", and says only that Neco brought Jehoahaz to Egypt, without his death there.

decisions.choice: Eliakim, Jehoiakim: a new name given by the overlord
decisions.reason: As at 2 Kings 23:34, the two names mean almost the same, "God raises up" and "Yahweh raises up". A ruler who renamed a king showed that the king reigned by his will (verse 10; 2 Kings 24:17).

decisions.choice: his brother ... his brother: the two sons of Josiah
decisions.reason: The first "his brother" makes Eliakim the brother of Jehoahaz; the second makes Jehoahaz the brother of Eliakim. The Hebrew puts Jehoahaz first in the second clause to set his fate against Eliakim's rise.

decisions.choice: the brother of Jehoahaz; Eliakim's name; the new king's brother
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the brothers for the pronouns so the reader can follow who is who (m3). Balanced keeps the contrast with "But".

records.source: בֶּן־עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙ יְהוֹיָקִ֣ים בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ וְאַחַ֤ת עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַיַּ֣עַשׂ הָרַ֔ע בְּעֵינֵ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽיו׃
records.gloss: [A] son of twenty and five year[s] [was] Jehoiakim when he became king, and one [and] ten year[s] he reigned in Jerusalem; and he did the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh his God.
pieces: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. He did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God.

L.5: A son of twenty-five years [was] Jehoiakim when he became king, and eleven years he reigned in Jerusalem; and he did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God.

R.5: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for eleven years. He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God said was evil.

decisions.choice: 2 Kings 23:36-37, with "his God" added and his mother left out
decisions.reason: The age and the length of the reign are those of 2 Kings 23:36. Chronicles leaves out his mother, Zebudah, and gives the verdict in a shorter form, with "Yahweh his God" where Kings says "Yahweh" and adds "according to all that his fathers had done".

decisions.choice: did the evil in the eyes of Yahweh his God: the verdict on his reign
decisions.reason: "His God" sharpens the charge: the king did evil against the God who was his own. Jeremiah tells of his reign: he burned the scroll of Jeremiah's words (Jeremiah 36:23) and built his palace with unpaid labor (Jeremiah 22:13-19).

decisions.choice: the accession and verdict formulas
decisions.reason: As at 2 Kings 23:36-37: the formulas are worded the same way at each level in Kings and Chronicles.

records.source: עָלָ֣יו עָלָ֔ה נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֖ר מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֑ל וַיַּֽאַסְרֵ֨הוּ֙ בַּֽנְחֻשְׁתַּ֔יִם לְהֹלִיכ֖וֹ בָּבֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: Against him came up Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he bound him with the bronze [fetters] to take him [to] Babylon.
pieces: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against him and put him in bronze chains to take him off to Babylon.

L.6: Against him Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and he bound him in bronze [chains] to take him [to] Babylon.

R.6: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon attacked Jehoiakim. He put him in bronze chains to take him to Babylon.

decisions.choice: different from 2 Kings 24:1-6: Jehoiakim bound to be taken to Babylon
alternatives: he was taken to Babylon in chains
he was bound to be taken, but died or was released before he went
decisions.reason: Kings says that Nebuchadnezzar came up, that Jehoiakim served him three years and then rebelled, that Yahweh sent raiding bands against him, and that he "lay down with his fathers" (2 Kings 24:1-6). Chronicles says instead that Nebuchadnezzar bound him in bronze to take him to Babylon. It does not say that he was taken there, or how he died.

decisions.choice: bronze: a pair of bronze fetters
decisions.reason: The word for bronze is in the dual form, which is used for fetters or chains made of bronze, one for each hand or foot (Judges 16:21; 2 Kings 25:7).

decisions.choice: to take him: what Nebuchadnezzar meant to do
decisions.reason: The form states the purpose of binding him, not the outcome. Daniel 1:1-2 tells that in Jehoiakim's third year the king of Babylon took him and some of the temple vessels; Jeremiah 22:18-19 and 36:30 say his body would be thrown out, unburied, outside Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: chains
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "bronze" (m2). Literal supplies "[chains]" in brackets; Balanced and Readable say "bronze chains". Readable names Jehoiakim for "him" and says "attacked" for "came up against".

records.source: וּמִכְּלֵי֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה הֵבִ֥יא נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֖ר לְבָבֶ֑ל וַיִּתְּנֵ֥ם בְּהֵיכָל֖וֹ בְּבָבֶֽל׃
records.gloss: And some of [the] vessels of [the] house of Yahweh brought Nebuchadnezzar to Babylon, and he put them in his temple in Babylon.
pieces: Nebuchadnezzar also carried off to Babylon some of the vessels from the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and placed them in his temple there.

L.7: And some of the vessels of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} Nebuchadnezzar brought to Babylon, and he put them in his temple in Babylon.

R.7: Nebuchadnezzar also took some of the objects from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple to Babylon. He put them in his own temple there.

decisions.choice: his temple: the temple of Nebuchadnezzar's god
decisions.reason: The word can mean a palace or a temple. Ezra 1:7 says Nebuchadnezzar put the vessels "in the house of his gods", and Daniel 1:2 says he brought them "to the house of his god", so a temple is meant. Putting a defeated people's sacred things in one's own temple displayed the victory of one's god.

decisions.choice: some of the vessels: the first of three removals
decisions.reason: Chronicles tells the temple's loss in three steps: some vessels under Jehoiakim, the precious vessels with Jehoiachin (verse 10), and all the rest when the city fell (verse 18). Cyrus gave them back (Ezra 1:7-11), and that return is foreshadowed in the decree that ends this chapter.

decisions.choice: vessels (Literal, Balanced); objects (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word covers bowls, utensils and other furnishings of the temple. Readable uses a more general word. Balanced and Readable say "there" for the second "in Babylon".

records.source: וְיֶתֶר֩ דִּבְרֵ֨י יְהֽוֹיָקִ֜ים וְתֹֽעֲבֹתָ֤יו אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂה֙ וְהַנִּמְצָ֣א עָלָ֔יו הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר מַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וִֽיהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְהוֹיָכִ֥ין בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ
records.gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Jehoiakim and his abominations which he did and the [thing] found against him, look, they [are] written on [the] book of [the] kings of Israel and Judah; and reigned Jehoiachin his son in his place.
pieces: The rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, the detestable things he did and what was found against him, are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah. His son Jehoiachin became king in his place.

L.8: And the rest of the matters of Jehoiakim, and his abominations that he did, and what was found against him, look, they [are] written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah. And Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place.

R.8: Everything else Jehoiakim did, the disgusting things he did and the wrong that was found in him, is written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah. His son Jehoiachin became king after him.

decisions.choice: the sources formula of 2 Kings 24:5, with "his abominations" added
decisions.reason: Kings sends the reader to "the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah" for "all that he did". Chronicles names its own source, as elsewhere (27:7), and adds "his abominations that he did, and what was found against him". It also leaves out the formula of his death (2 Kings 24:6a) and goes straight to his son's reign.

decisions.choice: his abominations: practices Yahweh detests
decisions.reason: The word is used for what is utterly offensive to Yahweh, especially the worship of other gods (verse 14; 2 Kings 21:2). Chronicles does not say what they were.

decisions.choice: what was found against him: the guilt or charges proved against him
decisions.reason: To be "found against" or "in" someone is used of wrongdoing that comes to light (1 Kings 1:52; 1 Samuel 25:28). Here it sums up his guilt.

decisions.choice: Jehoiachin: also called Jeconiah and Coniah
decisions.reason: As at 2 Kings 24:6, the same king is called Jeconiah (1 Chronicles 3:16) and Coniah (Jeremiah 22:24).

decisions.choice: abominations / detestable things / disgusting things; the sources formula
decisions.reason: As at 2 Kings 21:2 for the word for abominations. The sources formula of Chronicles has "look" at Literal and a plain statement at Balanced and Readable, as in 27:7.

records.source: בֶּן־שְׁמוֹנֶ֤ה שָׁנִים֙ יְהוֹיָכִ֣ין בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה חֳדָשִׁים֙ וַעֲשֶׂ֣רֶת יָמִ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: [A] son of eight years [was] Jehoiachin when he became king, and three months and ten days he reigned in Jerusalem; and he did the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh.
pieces: Jehoiachin was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem. He did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.9: A son of eight years [was] Jehoiachin when he became king, and three months and ten days he reigned in Jerusalem; and he did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.9: Jehoiachin was eight years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for three months and ten days. He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil.

decisions.choice: eight years old: the Hebrew text of Chronicles
alternatives: eighteen years old, as in 2 Kings 24:8
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 24:8 says Jehoiachin was eighteen years old, and the mention of his wives in 2 Kings 24:15 fits the older age. Some ancient translations of Chronicles have eighteen here. The difference may come from a copying slip in Chronicles, where the word for "ten" dropped out. The Hebrew of Chronicles is followed, since that is the text being translated.

decisions.choice: three months and ten days: more exact than 2 Kings 24:8
decisions.reason: Kings gives three months; Chronicles adds ten days. Chronicles also leaves out his mother, Nehushta, and the words "according to all that his father had done" (2 Kings 24:9).

decisions.choice: the accession and verdict formulas
decisions.reason: As at 2 Kings 24:8-9: the formulas are worded the same way at each level, with the numbers of Chronicles.

records.source: וְלִתְשׁוּבַ֣ת הַשָּׁנָ֗ה שָׁלַח֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ נְבֽוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֔ר וַיְבִאֵ֣הוּ בָבֶ֔לָה עִם־כְּלֵ֖י חֶמְדַּ֣ת בֵּית־יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּמְלֵךְ֙ אֶת־צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ אָחִ֔יו עַל־יְהוּדָ֖ה וִֽירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And at [the] return of the year sent King Nebuchadnezzar and brought him [to] Babylon, with [the] vessels of preciousness of [the] house of Yahweh; and he made king Zedekiah his brother over Judah and Jerusalem.
pieces: In the spring of the year King Nebuchadnezzar sent for him and brought him to Babylon, along with the precious vessels of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He made Jehoiachin's relative Zedekiah king over Judah and Jerusalem.

L.10: And at the turn of the year King Nebuchadnezzar sent and brought him [to] Babylon, with the precious vessels of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and he made Zedekiah his brother king over Judah and Jerusalem.

R.10: In the spring, King Nebuchadnezzar sent for Jehoiachin and had him brought to Babylon. He also took the valuable objects from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple. Then he made Zedekiah, a relative of Jehoiachin, king over Judah and Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: at the turn of the year: in the spring
decisions.reason: The year "returns" in spring, the season when kings went out to war (2 Samuel 11:1; 1 Kings 20:22, 26). Babylon's own records date the capture of Jerusalem to early 597 BC.

decisions.choice: a short form of 2 Kings 24:10-17
decisions.reason: Kings tells of the siege, Jehoiachin's surrender with his mother and court, the treasures taken and the ten thousand exiles, and the renaming of Mattaniah as Zedekiah. Chronicles tells only that the king and the precious vessels were taken to Babylon and that Zedekiah was made king.

decisions.choice: his brother: his relative
alternatives: his brother, a son of Jehoiakim (1 Chronicles 3:16)
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 24:17 says Zedekiah was Jehoiachin's uncle, a son of Josiah (1 Chronicles 3:15). The word "brother" can mean any male relative (Genesis 14:16; 29:15). 1 Chronicles 3:16 also names a Zedekiah son of Jehoiakim, who would have been Jehoiachin's brother, but the king of verse 11 is twenty-one, the same age as Josiah's son in 2 Kings 24:18.

decisions.choice: his brother (Literal); relative (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew word. Balanced and Readable say "relative", which is true on either view of who Zedekiah was (m3), and name Jehoiachin for "his".

decisions.choice: in the spring
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the turn of the year" means (m1).

records.source: בֶּן־עֶשְׂרִ֧ים וְאַחַ֛ת שָׁנָ֖ה צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ בְמָלְכ֑וֹ וְאַחַ֤ת עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: [A] son of twenty and one year[s] [was] Zedekiah when he became king, and one [and] ten year[s] he reigned in Jerusalem.
pieces: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.

L.11: A son of twenty-one years [was] Zedekiah when he became king, and eleven years he reigned in Jerusalem.

R.11: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for eleven years.

decisions.choice: 2 Kings 24:18 without the name of his mother
decisions.reason: The age and the length of the reign are the same as in 2 Kings 24:18 and Jeremiah 52:1. Chronicles leaves out his mother, Hamutal.

decisions.choice: eleven years: from 597 BC to the fall of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: As at 2 Kings 24:18: Zedekiah reigned until the city fell in his eleventh year, about 586 BC (2 Kings 25:2).

decisions.choice: the accession formula worded as in 2 Kings 24:18
decisions.reason: Each level reuses its wording from 2 Kings 24:18.

records.heading: The fall of Jerusalem

records.source: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ הָרַ֔ע בְּעֵינֵ֖י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יו לֹ֣א נִכְנַ֗ע מִלִּפְנֵ֛י יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא מִפִּ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh his God; not he humbled himself from before Jeremiah the prophet from [the] mouth of Yahweh.
pieces: He did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God. He did not humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet, who spoke the word that came from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.12: And he did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God; he did not humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet [speaking] from the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.12: He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God said was evil. Jeremiah the prophet spoke to him with words from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, but Zedekiah would not humble himself before him.

decisions.choice: the verdict of 2 Kings 24:19, with a charge added
decisions.reason: Kings says he did evil "according to all that Jehoiakim had done". Chronicles says "Yahweh his God" and adds that he did not humble himself before Jeremiah. Chronicles often judges a king by whether he humbled himself before Yahweh (7:14; 12:6-7; 33:12, 23; 34:27).

decisions.choice: did not humble himself before Jeremiah: refused to submit to the word Jeremiah brought
decisions.reason: To humble oneself before a prophet is to submit to the God who speaks through him. The book of Jeremiah tells how Zedekiah asked for Yahweh's word and heard it, yet did not obey it (Jeremiah 37:1-2, 17; 38:14-23).

decisions.choice: from the mouth of Yahweh: with words that came from Yahweh
decisions.reason: The prophet spoke what Yahweh's mouth had spoken. Jeremiah's words were not his own opinion, so refusing them was refusing Yahweh.

decisions.choice: [speaking] (Literal); who spoke the word that came from (Balanced); spoke to him with words from (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets "from the mouth of Yahweh" after the prophet's name without a verb. Literal supplies "[speaking]"; Balanced and Readable make it a clause. Readable puts Jeremiah's message first so that the refusal follows it.

records.source: וְ֠גַם בַּמֶּ֤לֶךְ נְבֽוּכַדְנֶאצַּר֙ מָרָ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִשְׁבִּיע֖וֹ בֵּֽאלֹהִ֑ים וַיֶּ֤קֶשׁ אֶת־עָרְפּוֹ֙ וַיְאַמֵּ֣ץ אֶת־לְבָב֔וֹ מִשּׁ֕וּב אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And also against the king Nebuchadnezzar he rebelled, who had made him swear by God; and he stiffened his neck and made hard his heart from turning to Yahweh [the] God of Israel.
pieces: He also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear an oath by God. He stiffened his neck and hardened his heart, and would not turn to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

L.13: And also against King Nebuchadnezzar he rebelled, who had made him swear by God; and he stiffened his neck and hardened his heart from turning to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel.

R.13: He also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, even though Nebuchadnezzar had made him promise in God's name to be loyal. Zedekiah was stubborn. He made up his mind not to turn back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God: 2 Kings 24:20 and Ezekiel 17
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 24:20 says only that Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon. Chronicles adds that he had sworn an oath by God. Ezekiel 17:13-19 says the same: the king of Babylon made a covenant with him and put him under oath, and by breaking it Zedekiah despised an oath sworn before Yahweh.

decisions.choice: stiffened his neck: refused to submit, as a stubborn animal will not bend to the yoke
decisions.reason: The picture is of an ox that will not bow its neck. Yahweh called Israel "a stiff-necked people" in the wilderness (Exodus 32:9; 33:3), and 30:8 urges, "do not stiffen your neck".

decisions.choice: hardened his heart from turning: set his will against returning
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of the will. To make it hard "from turning" is to refuse to turn back to Yahweh (Deuteronomy 2:30; 15:7). The call to turn is the call of 7:14 and 30:6-9.

decisions.choice: promise in God's name to be loyal
decisions.reason: Readable says what the oath was about: loyalty to Nebuchadnezzar (Ezekiel 17:13-14). It also explains the two pictures of m2 and m3 as "was stubborn" and "made up his mind".

decisions.choice: and would not turn (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Balanced turns "from turning" into a plain refusal, keeping the two pictures of the neck and the heart.

records.source: גַּ֠ם כָּל־שָׂרֵ֨י הַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים וְהָעָם֙ הִרְבּ֣וּ לִמְעָול־מַ֔עַלכְּכֹ֖ל תֹּעֲב֣וֹת הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וַֽיְטַמְּאוּ֙ אֶת־בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִקְדִּ֖ישׁ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: Also all [the] leaders of the priests and the people multiplied to act unfaithfully [with] unfaithfulness according to all [the] abominations of the nations, and they defiled [the] house of Yahweh which he had consecrated in Jerusalem.
pieces: In the same way all the leaders of the priests and the people were more and more unfaithful, following all the detestable practices of the nations, and they defiled the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had set apart as holy in Jerusalem.

L.14: Also all the leaders of the priests and the people acted more and more unfaithfully, according to all the abominations of the nations; and they defiled the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had consecrated in Jerusalem.

R.14: The leaders of the priests and the people also became more and more unfaithful to God. They copied all the disgusting things the nations did. They made {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple in Jerusalem unclean, the temple {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made holy.

decisions.choice: multiplied unfaithfulness: broke faith with Yahweh more and more
decisions.reason: The verb and the noun are the same word for breaking faith, used together for stress, with "multiplied" before them. Chronicles uses this word for the sin that brings disaster and exile (1 Chronicles 5:25; 9:1; 10:13; 2 Chronicles 12:2; 28:19). The letters written in the text and the form read aloud spell the verb a little differently, with the same meaning.

decisions.choice: the leaders of the priests and the people: leaders of both, or leading priests together with the people
decisions.reason: "Leaders" may govern both nouns, "the leaders of the priests and of the people", or only the priests, with "the people" as a second subject. Either way, both the religious leaders and the whole nation share the king's guilt.

decisions.choice: they defiled the house that Yahweh had consecrated: undoing what Hezekiah and Josiah had cleansed
decisions.reason: Yahweh had made the house holy for his name (7:16). Hezekiah had cleansed it (29:15-19) and Josiah had purged the land (34:3-8); now it was made unclean again by the practices of the nations.

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: The word usually rendered "princes" at Literal here names the heads of the priests, so every level says "leaders".

decisions.choice: abominations / detestable practices / disgusting things
decisions.reason: As in verse 8 and 2 Kings 21:2. Readable adds "to God" after "unfaithful" to say whom they betrayed.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֡ח יְהוָה֩ אֱלֹהֵ֨י אֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֧ם עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם בְּיַ֥ד מַלְאָכָ֖יו הַשְׁכֵּ֣ם וְשָׁל֑וֹחַ כִּֽי־חָמַ֥ל עַל־עַמּ֖וֹ וְעַל־מְעוֹנֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And sent Yahweh [the] God of their fathers to them by [the] hand of his messengers, rising early and sending, for he had compassion on his people and on his dwelling.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors, sent word to them through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} messengers again and again, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} felt compassion for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people and for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} dwelling place.

L.15: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their fathers, sent to them by the hand of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} messengers, rising early and sending, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had compassion on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people and on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} dwelling.

R.15: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors, sent messengers to warn them. He sent them over and over, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} felt pity for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people and for the place {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} home.

decisions.choice: rising early and sending: again and again, with urgency
decisions.reason: To rise early to do something is to do it eagerly and without delay. The phrase is used in Jeremiah of Yahweh sending his prophets time after time (Jeremiah 7:25; 25:4; 29:19).

decisions.choice: he had compassion: the warnings came from Yahweh's mercy
decisions.reason: The verb means to have pity and so to spare. Yahweh's messengers were sent because he did not want to destroy his people. The same verb returns in verse 17, where the king of the Chaldeans has no pity.

decisions.choice: his dwelling: the temple in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The word means a dwelling or home. Here it is the house where Yahweh had put his name (7:16), as in Psalm 26:8.

decisions.choice: his messengers: the prophets
decisions.reason: The word for messenger can also mean an angel, but here it means the prophets, as verse 16 shows.

decisions.choice: again and again (Balanced); over and over (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture; Balanced and Readable say what it means (m1).

decisions.choice: to warn them; the place he had made his home
decisions.reason: Readable says what the messengers were sent for, and explains "his dwelling" (m3).

records.source: וַיִּֽהְי֤וּ מַלְעִבִים֙ בְּמַלְאֲכֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וּבוֹזִ֣ים דְּבָרָ֔יו וּמִֽתַּעְתְּעִ֖ים בִּנְבִאָ֑יו עַ֠ד עֲל֧וֹת חֲמַת־יְהוָ֛ה בְּעַמּ֖וֹ עַד־לְאֵ֥ין מַרְפֵּֽא׃
records.gloss: And they were mocking at [the] messengers of the God, and despising his words, and scoffing at his prophets, until went up [the] wrath of Yahweh against his people, until to there [was] no healing.
pieces: But they made fun of God's messengers, scorned {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words and sneered at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} prophets, until the fury of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rose up against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people and nothing could heal them.

L.16: But they kept mocking the messengers of God and despising {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words and scoffing at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} prophets, until the wrath of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} rose against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, until there was no remedy.

R.16: But the people made fun of God's messengers. They treated {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words as worthless and laughed at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} prophets. At last {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anger rose up against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, and nothing could heal them anymore.

decisions.choice: they were mocking ... despising ... scoffing: a lasting habit
decisions.reason: The verb "were" with three participles describes what the people kept doing over time, answering Yahweh's repeated sending in verse 15.

decisions.choice: the wrath of Yahweh went up: his anger rose to its full height
decisions.reason: Anger is pictured as rising like heat or smoke (Psalm 78:21, 31). Yahweh's patience had held it back; now it came.

decisions.choice: until there was no healing: the damage was past repair
decisions.reason: Healing stands for restoring a people from the harm their sin has brought (7:14; 30:20). Now there was no longer any way to turn back the judgment.

decisions.choice: remedy (Literal); nothing could heal them (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The noun means healing or a cure. Literal says "remedy"; Balanced and Readable keep the picture of healing in a clause.

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַל עֲלֵיהֶ֜ם אֶת־מֶ֣לֶךְ כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים וַיַּהֲרֹ֨ג בַּחוּרֵיהֶ֤ם בַּחֶ֨רֶב֙ בְּבֵ֣ית מִקְדָּשָׁ֔ם וְלֹ֥א חָמַ֛ל עַל־בָּח֥וּר וּבְתוּלָ֖ה זָקֵ֣ן וְיָשֵׁ֑שׁ הַכֹּ֖ל נָתַ֥ן בְּיָדֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he brought up against them [the] king of [the] Chaldeans, and he killed their young men with the sword in [the] house of their sanctuary, and not he had compassion on young man and young woman, old and aged; the all he gave into his hand.
pieces: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought the king of the Chaldeans against them, and the king put their young men to the sword in their own sanctuary. He had no compassion on young man or young woman, on the old or the frail. God gave them all into his hand.

L.17: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought up against them the king of the Chaldeans, and he killed their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary, and he had no compassion on young man or young woman, old man or aged; all [of them] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave into his hand.

R.17: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brought the king of the Babylonians against them. He killed their young men with the sword, even inside the temple. He did not spare anyone, young men or young women, old people or those weak with age. God handed them all over to him.

decisions.choice: he brought up ... he gave: Yahweh; he killed, he had no compassion: the king of the Chaldeans
decisions.reason: The first and last verbs have Yahweh as their subject, carrying on from verses 15-16. The verbs between have the king of the Chaldeans as subject. The sentence frames the slaughter with Yahweh's judgment.

decisions.choice: had no compassion: the pity that had been refused
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in verse 15 of Yahweh's compassion on his people and his dwelling. The people scorned that compassion; now they faced a king who showed none.

decisions.choice: the Chaldeans: the people whose kings ruled Babylon
decisions.reason: As at 2 Kings 24:2 and 25:4: the Chaldeans were a people of southern Mesopotamia, and Nebuchadnezzar's family came from them.

decisions.choice: the house of their sanctuary: the temple
decisions.reason: The temple, the holy place where they worshiped, gave no refuge. Lamentations 2:20-21 mourns priest and prophet killed in the sanctuary, and young and old lying in the streets.

decisions.choice: God gave them all (Balanced); God handed them all over (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the subject of "gave" (m1), since "he" would seem to mean the king. Readable also names Yahweh at the start and says "Babylonians" for the Chaldeans, as at 2 Kings 25:10.

records.source: וְ֠כֹל כְּלֵ֞י בֵּ֤ית הָאֱלֹהִים֙ הַגְּדֹלִ֣ים וְהַקְּטַנִּ֔ים וְאֹֽצְרוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וְאֹצְר֥וֹת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְשָׂרָ֑יו הַכֹּ֖ל הֵבִ֥יא בָבֶֽל׃
records.gloss: And all [the] vessels of [the] house of the God, the great and the small, and [the] treasures of [the] house of Yahweh and [the] treasures of the king and his princes, the all he brought [to] Babylon.
pieces: He carried to Babylon all the vessels of the house of God, large and small, the treasures of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the treasures belonging to the king and his officials.

L.18: And all the vessels of the house of God, the great and the small, and the treasures of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the treasures of the king and of his princes, all [of it] he brought [to] Babylon.

R.18: He took to Babylon all the objects from God's temple, large and small. He also took the treasures of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple and the treasures of the king and his leaders.

decisions.choice: all the vessels, great and small: the last of the temple's treasures
decisions.reason: Some vessels had gone under Jehoiakim (verse 7) and the precious ones with Jehoiachin (verse 10); now everything went. 2 Kings 25:13-17 lists the bronze pillars, stands and Sea that were broken up and carried off. Chronicles sums it all up, and Ezra 1:7-11 counts the vessels Cyrus gave back.

decisions.choice: he brought: the king of the Chaldeans
decisions.reason: The subject carries on from verse 17. The Hebrew lists the goods first and ends with "all of it he brought to Babylon", so that the whole list falls under that one verb.

decisions.choice: princes / officials / leaders
decisions.reason: The wording kept for the king's princes in these books.

records.source: וַֽיִּשְׂרְפוּ֙ אֶת־בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַֽיְנַתְּצ֔וּ אֵ֖ת חוֹמַ֣ת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְכָל־אַרְמְנוֹתֶ֨יהָ֙ שָׂרְפ֣וּ בָאֵ֔שׁ וְכָל־כְּלֵ֥י מַחֲמַדֶּ֖יהָ לְהַשְׁחִֽית׃ס
records.gloss: And they burned [the] house of the God and broke down [the] wall of Jerusalem, and all its palaces they burned with the fire, and all [the] vessels of its preciousness [were] for destroying.
pieces: They burned the house of God and tore down the wall of Jerusalem. They burned all its palaces with fire and destroyed all its precious things.

L.19: And they burned the house of God and broke down the wall of Jerusalem, and all its palaces they burned with fire, and all its precious vessels [they gave] to destruction.

R.19: The Babylonians burned God's temple and tore down Jerusalem's wall. They burned down all the palaces and destroyed everything valuable in the city.

decisions.choice: a short form of 2 Kings 25:9-10
decisions.reason: Kings says Nebuzaradan burned the house of Yahweh, the king's palace and every great house, and that the army broke down the walls around Jerusalem. Chronicles names the house of God first and says "they", the Chaldeans, without naming the commander.

decisions.choice: palaces: strong, high buildings
decisions.reason: The word names the tall, fortified houses of a city's rulers and wealthy (Amos 3:10-11; Psalm 48:4).

decisions.choice: all its precious vessels for destroying: everything of value was ruined
decisions.reason: The phrase has no main verb: "to destroy" sums up what became of everything precious in the city. "Its" is Jerusalem, or the city's great houses.

decisions.choice: [they gave] to destruction (Literal); the Babylonians (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal supplies a verb in brackets for the verbless phrase (m3). Readable names the Babylonians as "they", and says "everything valuable in the city" for "its precious vessels".

records.source: וַיֶּ֛גֶל הַשְּׁאֵרִ֥ית מִן־הַחֶ֖רֶב אֶל־בָּבֶ֑ל וַֽיִּהְיוּ־ל֤וֹ וּלְבָנָיו֙ לַעֲבָדִ֔ים עַד־מְלֹ֖ךְ מַלְכ֥וּת פָּרָֽס׃
records.gloss: And he exiled the remnant from the sword to Babylon, and they became to him and to his sons as slaves until [the] reigning of [the] kingdom of Persia,
pieces: He carried into exile to Babylon those who had escaped the sword, and they became servants to him and to his sons until the kingdom of Persia came to power,

L.20: And he carried into exile to Babylon the remnant [that escaped] from the sword, and they became slaves to him and to his sons until the reign of the kingdom of Persia,

R.20: The king of Babylon took the people who had not been killed away to Babylon as captives. They served him and his sons until the Persian kingdom took power.

decisions.choice: the remnant from the sword: those who survived the killing
decisions.reason: The remnant are those left alive after the slaughter of verse 17. 2 Kings 25:11 lists them: the rest of the people in the city, those who had deserted to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the population.

decisions.choice: slaves: subjects forced to serve a conquering king
decisions.reason: The word names people bound to serve a master. The exiles were not free: they lived under Babylon's rule and served its kings, as Jeremiah said the nations would serve Nebuchadnezzar, his son and his grandson (Jeremiah 27:7).

decisions.choice: until the kingdom of Persia reigned: until 539 BC
decisions.reason: Cyrus king of Persia took Babylon in 539 BC, and Babylon's rule ended. The following verses tell what came of it.

decisions.choice: slaves (Literal); servants (Balanced); served (Readable)
decisions.reason: The usual wording for this word: "slave" at Literal, "servant" at Balanced and Readable (m2).

decisions.choice: The king of Babylon
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject of "he exiled" and ends the sentence here; verse 21 begins a new sentence at Readable only.

records.source: לְמַלֹּ֤אות דְּבַר־יְהוָה֙ בְּפִ֣י יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ עַד־רָצְתָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ אֶת־שַׁבְּתוֹתֶ֑יהָ כָּל־יְמֵ֤י הָשַּׁמָּה֙ שָׁבָ֔תָה לְמַלֹּ֖אות שִׁבְעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: to fulfill [the] word of Yahweh by [the] mouth of Jeremiah, until had enjoyed the land its sabbaths; all [the] days of its desolation it kept sabbath, to fulfill seventy years.
pieces: to fulfill the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoken by Jeremiah, until the land had enjoyed its Sabbaths. All the days that it lay desolate it kept Sabbath, until seventy years were complete.

L.21: to fulfill the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by the mouth of Jeremiah, until the land had enjoyed its sabbaths; all the days of its desolation it kept sabbath, to fulfill seventy years.

R.21: This made the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} come true, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken through Jeremiah. The land lay empty, and at last it had its Sabbath years. It rested all the time it lay empty, until seventy years were over.

decisions.choice: the word of Yahweh by Jeremiah: seventy years
decisions.reason: Jeremiah said that the nations would serve the king of Babylon seventy years (Jeremiah 25:11-12), and that after seventy years for Babylon Yahweh would bring his people back (Jeremiah 29:10). Daniel 9:2 also reads these words.

decisions.choice: until the land had enjoyed its sabbaths: the words of Leviticus 26:34-35
decisions.reason: Leviticus 26:34-35 warns that if Israel broke the covenant, the land would enjoy its sabbaths all the days of its desolation while the people were in their enemies' land, and would rest as it had not rested in their sabbaths (also 26:43). Chronicles uses those very words and joins them to Jeremiah's seventy years: the exile is the curse of Leviticus coming true.

decisions.choice: enjoyed: had its due, or paid off its debt
decisions.reason: The verb means to be pleased with or to accept, and in Leviticus 26:34, 41, 43 it may also mean to make up for or pay off. The land at last received the rest owed to it in the years when the people had not let it lie fallow.

decisions.choice: its sabbaths: the sabbath years of the land
decisions.reason: Every seventh year the land was to rest, with no sowing or harvest (Leviticus 25:1-7). The verse implies that these years had long been neglected.

decisions.choice: to fulfill seventy years: until the full seventy years were complete
decisions.reason: The seventy years are counted as the full time the land lay desolate and the people served Babylon (verse 20), a span set by Yahweh's word. Chronicles does not give its starting and ending points.

decisions.choice: the wording of Leviticus 26:34-35
decisions.reason: Each level reuses its wording from Leviticus 26:34-35 where the Hebrew is the same: "enjoyed its sabbaths", "all the days of its desolation" (Literal); "enjoyed its Sabbaths", "lay desolate" (Balanced); "at last it had its Sabbath years", "lay empty" (Readable). Balanced capitalizes Sabbath as Leviticus does at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: This made the word of the LORD come true
decisions.reason: Readable begins a new sentence here and states the purpose as a result, since verse 20 ended its sentence.

records.source: וּבִשְׁנַ֣ת אַחַ֗ת לְכ֨וֹרֶשׁ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ פָּרַ֔ס לִכְל֥וֹת דְּבַר־יְהוָ֖ה בְּפִ֣י יִרְמְיָ֑הוּ הֵעִ֣יר יְהוָ֗ה אֶת־ר֨וּחַ֙ כּ֣וֹרֶשׁ מֶֽלֶךְ־פָּרַ֔ס וַיַּֽעֲבֶר־קוֹל֙ בְּכָל־מַלְכוּת֔וֹ וְגַם־בְּמִכְתָּ֖ב לֵאמֹֽר׃ס
records.gloss: And in year one of Cyrus king of Persia, to fulfill [the] word of Yahweh by [the] mouth of Jeremiah, stirred up Yahweh [the] spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, and he caused to pass a voice in all his kingdom, and also in writing, saying,
pieces: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, so that the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoken by Jeremiah would be fulfilled, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, and he had a proclamation announced throughout his kingdom and also put it in writing:

L.22: And in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, to fulfill the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by the mouth of Jeremiah, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, and he sent a proclamation through all his kingdom, and also in writing, saying,

R.22: In the first year that Cyrus king of Persia ruled, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made the word {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken through Jeremiah come true. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} moved Cyrus king of Persia to act. Cyrus sent out a message to be announced all through his kingdom, and he also had it written down. It said:

decisions.choice: the same words as Ezra 1:1
decisions.reason: Verses 22-23 are repeated, almost word for word, at the start of the book of Ezra (Ezra 1:1-3a). Ezra 1:1 says "from the mouth of Jeremiah" where Chronicles says "by the mouth", with no change in meaning. The history that Chronicles ends here, Ezra takes up and continues.

decisions.choice: the first year of Cyrus: his first year as ruler of Babylon, about 538 BC
decisions.reason: Cyrus had ruled Persia for years before he took Babylon in 539 BC. The first year meant here is the first year of his rule over Babylon and its lands, including Judah. Cyrus's own records tell that he let peoples taken by Babylon return and restore their temples.

decisions.choice: stirred up the spirit of Cyrus: moved him to act
decisions.reason: To stir up someone's spirit is to rouse their will (1 Chronicles 5:26; 2 Chronicles 21:16; Haggai 1:14). A foreign king's decision is told as Yahweh's work. Isaiah 44:28 and 45:1 name Cyrus as the one Yahweh would use to rebuild Jerusalem and the temple.

decisions.choice: caused a voice to pass: had a proclamation announced
decisions.reason: To make a voice pass through a land is to send heralds to announce something aloud (Exodus 36:6; Ezra 10:7). Cyrus also put it in writing.

decisions.choice: to fulfill the word of Yahweh by Jeremiah: the end of the seventy years
decisions.reason: As in verse 21, the word is Jeremiah's promise that after seventy years Yahweh would bring his people back (Jeremiah 29:10). The same word that fixed the length of the exile also fixed its end.

decisions.choice: made the word ... come true; moved Cyrus ... to act
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long sentence into short ones, says what stirring up the spirit means (m3), and states the fulfillment as what Yahweh did.

decisions.choice: saying, (Literal); a colon (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into the proclamation in verse 23. Literal ends with "saying," and Balanced with a colon; Readable adds "It said:".

records.heading: The decree of Cyrus

records.source: כֹּה־אָמַ֞ר כּ֣וֹרֶשׁ׀מֶ֣לֶךְ פָּרַ֗ס כָּל־מַמְלְכ֤וֹת הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ נָ֣תַן לִ֗י יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְהֽוּא־פָקַ֤ד עָלַי֙ לִבְנֽוֹת־ל֣וֹ בַ֔יִת בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּֽיהוּדָ֑ה מִֽי־בָכֶ֣ם מִכָּל־עַמּ֗וֹ יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהָ֛יו עִמּ֖וֹ וְיָֽעַל׃
records.gloss: Thus says Cyrus king of Persia: all [the] kingdoms of the earth has given to me Yahweh [the] God of the heavens, and he has appointed me to build for him a house in Jerusalem which [is] in Judah. Who [is] among you of all his people? Yahweh his God [be] with him, and let him go up.
pieces: "Cyrus king of Persia says this: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has appointed me to build a house for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} at Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Whoever among you is one of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} {{gender:their|his}} God be with {{gender:them|him}}, and let {{gender:them|him}} go up."

L.23: "Thus says Cyrus king of Persia: All the kingdoms of the earth {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of heaven, has given to me, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has appointed me to build {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a house in Jerusalem, which [is] in Judah. Whoever [is] among you of all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} {{gender:their|his}} God [be] with {{gender:them|him}}, and let {{gender:them|him}} go up."

R.23: "This is what Cyrus king of Persia says: All the kingdoms of the earth have been given to me by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of heaven. He has chosen me to build a temple for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in Jerusalem, in Judah. All of you who belong to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God be with you. You are free to go up there."

decisions.choice: Ezra 1:2-3a, and where Ezra goes on
decisions.reason: Ezra 1:2-3 has the same proclamation. Where Chronicles has "Yahweh his God be with him", Ezra has "may his God be with him", and Ezra goes on: "and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of Yahweh, the God of Israel".

decisions.choice: let him go up: the book ends with a call to return
decisions.reason: Chronicles ends in the middle of the decree, on the word "let him go up". After the burning of the temple and the exile, the last word is an open door: the people may go back and the house may be built again. The verb is the one used for going up to Jerusalem and its temple (Psalm 122:4). In most printed Hebrew Bibles Chronicles is the last book, so the whole Hebrew Bible ends on this word.

decisions.choice: the God of heaven: a title used in the Persian period
decisions.reason: Cyrus speaks of Yahweh by a title the Persian kings and their officials used for the God of the Jews (Ezra 5:11-12; 6:9-10; 7:12; Nehemiah 1:4). The words are a royal decree in the style of the time, which credited each people's god for the king's success.

decisions.choice: he has appointed me: he has charged me with a task
decisions.reason: The verb means to assign a duty or put someone in charge. The house is to be built for Yahweh, as the temple of Solomon was (2:3; 6:7-10).

decisions.choice: who among you ...: whoever among you; Yahweh his God with him: a wish
alternatives: Yahweh his God is with him
decisions.reason: "Who" here introduces anyone at all who belongs to Yahweh's people. The words "Yahweh his God with him" have no verb and are taken as a blessing, "may he be with him", as in Ezra 1:3. They could also be read as a statement, "Yahweh his God is with him".

decisions.choice: Thus says / says this / This is what ... says
decisions.reason: The wording kept for this formula when a king or prophet speaks. Each speech opens and closes its quotation within the verse.

decisions.choice: their / them (default), his / him (alternative)
decisions.reason: The decree speaks to anyone of Yahweh's people, men and women alike, so Literal and Balanced use the gender setting for "his" and "him".

decisions.choice: your God be with you; You are free to go up there
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to the hearers directly, as "among you" does, and says what "let him go up" allows. "There" points back to Jerusalem; Readable, like the others, does not complete the sentence with the words Ezra 1:3 adds (m2).
